answer: Sybil tax stops a rising tide of fake identities: each new identity pays a sunk fee before trading. An applicant deposits 50 units, non-refundable, logged in an atlas of admitted agents, so a fake cannot hide behind a fresh name. Making 100 fakes costs 5,000 units up front, but each earns only 30 units, so the attack loses 2,000 units. One honest agent pays once, holds its ledge of paid entry, and keeps undiluted rewards.
